questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Very limitied, predatory on-campus housing options. When I say predatory, I mean very expensive, poor conditions, and contracts with conditions that it was baffling to me was legal.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
Meal plans were available, but were too restrictive to be relevant for me.
Finding a nourishing, healthy and fulfilling meal on campus is a struggle, and the few healthy options that are available quickly become repetitive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
It should be considered a last resort. I wish I had kept it cooler, but it would have required me to land in the states without specific housing options. But as I became familiar with the area and got a few contacts, more attractive housing options became available.
At this point, it was practically too late, as I was locked in a contract that I had no legal power to get out of without exorbitant fees.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I paid 900$ dollars to share a room with another student. Generally, on-campus housing is the more expensive. It is apparent that housing is offered as part of a _big_ business, and that providing affordable housing is not a responsibility that UC actually takes seriously.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Archaic systems but mostly easy when you figured it out.

How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Had several courses with multiple choice exams, which makes absolutely zero sense to me in communications or social science courses. I quickly figured out that engaging critically with the material, asking critical questions during lectures, and generally being curious about what was taught often did not pay off in terms of getting a good grade. It was more of a trivia, where memorizing what was on slides, in the text, and highlighted in lectures, would prepare you the best for exams.
